Purpose and exclusions

Create new authored zones through catalogs, reusable Blueprint actors and content validation instead of changing C++ for every forest or town. Six region designs define a long-term world plan; they are not six finished 3D maps.

Never bypass the declared rule owner, mutate an authored definition at runtime, trust a client completion claim, or infer a compiled implementation from this page.

Creation and configuration

  1. Use File > New Level and the appropriate simple/open-world template after checking installed 5.8.3 behavior; start simple for the slice. Save to the registered Content/Game/Maps path.
  2. Author Landscape or modular 3D geometry, collision, PlayerStarts, NavMesh bounds, water regions, gate actors and safe hub. Use named folders in World Outliner for services/encounters/resources/entrances.
  3. Create the zone Data Asset and tables; register with URPGZoneCatalog and the backend zone allocator. Reopen neighboring gates for reciprocal destinations.
  4. Add minimap bounds, audio zones, climate definition, quest links and telemetry IDs. Keep routine content editable through Blueprint/Data Assets.
  5. Test interior entry/exit, bridge layers, slopes, swim shores, resource placement rejection and remote sprites before dressing with vegetation/buildings.

Required sequence: create native prerequisites -> actual build -> child/data creation -> configure -> assign to listed consumer -> save -> run named fixture. A compiled shell without its consumer assignment is not feature completion.

Functions, commands and event bindings

Project custom contracts are not engine/plugin nodes. A read-only asset participates through its consumer; it does not inherit that consumer’s mutation methods. Backend endpoint pages label transport proposals explicitly.

ContractExecution / effect

MeasureRoute(RouteId) -> TravelTimeSamples; QA procedure, not a fabricated benchmarkNative current owner; local request versus server validation as the command states. Backend work is asynchronous, cosmetics observe only after accepted state.

Lifecycle and cleanup

  1. Construct with only safe defaults; no service calls or world scans from construction scripts.
  2. Inject current owner/definition/session and subscribe once after readiness. Possession and replicated state may arrive in either order; guard initialization.
  3. Accept only permitted commands under current identity/epoch; keep local UI/cosmetic prediction separate from committed state.
  4. After server/backend result apply only matching request generation and nonstale revision; late reply to old body does not mutate new body.
  5. On death, transfer, disconnect, restart or teardown cancel transient work, clear input/timers, unbind delegates and release weak observers. Durable receipts remain authoritative.
  6. On reconnect create fresh runtime objects from current committed snapshot; never deserialize old Actor/widget pointers or rerun initial grants.

Concrete player-to-authority flow

Participation in Biome production, navigation, density and interiors. Rule owner: URPGZoneCatalog. This asset’s role is Create new authored zones through catalogs, reusable Blueprint actors and content validation instead of changing C++ for every forest or town. Six region designs define a long-term world plan; they are not six finished 3D maps.

  1. Start from the zone brief and adjacency graph; choose entrances and service placement before detailed art.
  2. Graybox landscape/roads/interiors with developer-owned simple meshes and scale markers; build collision/navigation and test capsule traversal.
  3. Register map/entrances/resources/water/NPC/encounter/quest/map-marker definitions with stable IDs. Run content validation and fix every missing reference.
  4. Add small encounter/resource populations, place service hub and one end-to-end quest route, then run two clients and transfer/reconnect tests.
  5. Measure travel times, navigation failures, resource/encounter density and client/server budgets. Only then replace graybox art and consider internal streaming.
  6. Package/cook the exact map references and content version; allocation refuses a server with mismatched catalogs. Expand in measured batches rather than claiming an endless world.

Named fixture and acceptance

Fixture: L_Morrowfen / Entrance_ReedRoad / ContentValidationFixture. Configure this asset at its first phase and run the linked phase recipe. Actual result: not run in Unreal/backend during documentation generation.

Stimulus / expected result
Missing return gate or invalid entrance -> catalog validation fails; zone not allocatable.
No navmesh on required route -> blocked production gate.
Resource quota places nodes in road -> reject candidate, not overlap buildings.
Map soft reference omitted from cook -> packaged admission fails in test; fix asset manager/cook inclusion before release.

Record expected/observed separately. Reopen the concrete map consumer; inspect authoritative state, stable IDs/revisions and UI. Static link checks cannot satisfy this gameplay test.

Common mistakes and staged limits

Do not duplicate a native rule in Blueprint, assume a planned type is compiled, or keep callbacks/owners valid after world or session replacement.

Do not build later references as empty shells in an earlier phase. Source-derived art rows remain blocked by the missing ZIP; plugin API bindings remain blocked by installed-source verification. Placeholder visuals and proposed tuning are explicitly not production proof.
